thread:
incident-bot: PAGER — GPU pool 'prod-us-east-1' EXHAUSTED. queue_size=12430, backlog_growth=+400/s. autoscaler attempted scale, reached max_replicas. immediate action required. TS=2162500000

deploy-bot: Heads up — model rollout v9.1 started at ~2162499900 to 60% traffic. rollout_id=r-2026-03-15-v9.1. No manual config changes noted in the rollout manifest.

ana (oncall): I'm taking this. seeing 504s spike and token throttles. top metric: latency p95->2.1s, queue length 12.4k. allocating logs now.

mike (eng-runtime): grabbing runtime logs — preliminary looks like kv-cache entries exploded after v9.1 due to much longer context windows. median sequence length jumped from ~512 to ~2048 over the last 30m. that increases per-request GPU memory dramatically.

sanjay (eng-sre): autoscaler tried to spin new GPU instances but got quota/softlimit errors: "max_replicas=40 reached" and some vendor-side provisioning latency/timeouts. new nodes coming up but many are failing healthchecks due to OOM during model init.

lucy (support): two paying customers (AcmeCorp, NovaRetail) reported generation failures and timeouts. both on Dedicated plans in us-east region. CS notified, they want ETA.

eve (product): did v9.1 change default context length or pre-processing? we didn't intentionally bump context in the release notes.

mike: v9.1 has changed tokenizer behavior for conversation mode — it preserves system+history tokens differently. effectively requests are 3-4x longer on average for some chat paths. kv-cache entries per session also increased. snippet from logs: ```ERROR kv_cache: entries=1_230_456 rss_bytes=127_345_678_912 model=v9.1 context_len=2048```

ana (oncall): mitigation proposal: 1) pause rollout / shift traffic back to v9.0 2) enable emergency burstpool (if possible) 3) raise autoscaler limit and request quota bump 4) short-term throttle long-context requests from public endpoints 5) customer communications. I'll start with pause.

deploy-bot: Command executed: ```redwoodctl rollout pause --model v9.1 --rollout r-2026-03-15-v9.1``` — traffic rollback to pinned-v9.0 in progress.

mike: while traffic shifts, we should also reduce model's max_context at the serving config to 1024 for v9.1 instances that are up, to avoid new heavy requests during warmup: ```serving-config: { model: v9.1, max_context: 1024 }``` — pushing change to canary nodes.

sanjay: enabling emergency burst pool now: requesting GPU-burst nodes and temporarily increasing node limit to 60. vendor side provisioning ETA ~8-12 minutes. note: some v9.1 instances will still fail init due to previously allocated KV sizes; we should drain failing nodes.

lucy: CS message drafted and sent to affected accounts: "We're aware of the generation failures in us-east affecting recent deployments. We've paused the rollout and are rolling traffic back to v9.0. We'll share updates in 30 minutes." kevin, please follow up on any immediate B2B escalations.

kevin (customer-success): on it — pinged AcmeCorp and NovaRetail. both ask for incident follow-up and any potential credit. collecting logs from them now.

ana (oncall): quick checklist: paused rollout (done), traffic shifted (in progress), throttling rules being applied, burstpool request sent, autoscale limit increased (pending vendor). handing to sanjay for infra steps and overnight monitoring.

sanjay: acknowledged. I'll own the handoff. immediate infra tasks: 1) drain failing instances 2) increase autoscale target to 60 3) add temporary iptables-based throttles for long-context endpoints: ```iptables -A INPUT -m string --algo bm --string "X-Context-Len:>1024" -j DROP``` (we'll implement via ingress proxy rule instead of iptables in prod).

mike: also enable kv-cache eviction policy more aggressively for v9.1 sessions: set eviction to LFU, ttl=60m for cold sessions. pushing config change now.

lucy: update for support: ticket numbers INC-2245 and INC-2246 created for AcmeCorp/NovaRetail. tagging SLA owners.

eve: product note — we need a rollback playbook for tokenizer-related regressions. also flag v9.1 for immediate postmortem and gate future rollouts with sequence-length histogram checks.

ana (oncall): handoff summary for night shift: paused v9.1 rollout; traffic rollback to v9.0 completed at +5m; applied temporary throttles; emergency burstpool requested; autoscaler max increased to 60 (pending); CS notified affected customers; SRE taking over. next steps: ensure queue drains below 1k, confirm latency stabilizes, schedule quota bump with cloud vendor.

sanjay: queued follow-ups: file vendor quota request (#VEND-789), collect heap dumps for failing nodes, rotate canary to new config with max_context=1024, and coordinate with Mike on kv-cache tuning. I've created a dedicated channel #inc-2162500000-kv-regress for the longform postmortem.

mike: observing queue length dropping from 12.4k -> 1.8k over 18 minutes after traffic shift and throttles. p95 latency returning to ~480ms. kv-cache entries trending down as eviction kicks in.

ana (oncall): thanks team. handing to SRE for overnight monitoring. I'll update the incident timeline and ETA for customers. Please dump any relevant logs into the incident folder.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — severity=high -> mitigated. impact: degraded generation in us-east for ~18 minutes, affected customers: 2 enterprise accounts, multiple self-serve requests throttled. next: postmortem in 72h. incident closed from pager perspective at TS=2162501200.
